description:
About the Position

The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in atmospheric sciences and oceanography, focused on machine-learning methods in climate modelling. The project applies modern data-driven techniques - from neural parameterisations to hybrid physics-ML modelling - to improve how climate models represent subgrid and coupled processes. The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment under the Swedish collective agreement, situated at the interface of climate physics and computational science.

Doctoral researchers in this area work with large climate-model datasets, design and train machine-learning components, and evaluate their impact on simulated climate within established model frameworks. The department collaborates with the Swedish national climate-research community and international model consortia, and candidates benefit from training in both atmospheric science and modern machine-learning practice, including access to national computing infrastructure.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in meteorology, physics, computer science or a related field, with demonstrated programming ability and interest in machine learning. Experience with deep-learning frameworks, large datasets or climate-model output is an advantage; a solid grounding in physical science is expected so that results can be interpreted physically. Applications run through the Varbi system with CV, transcripts, references and a statement of interest.

Highlights

  • PhD on machine learning for climate modelling at Stockholm MISU
  • Hybrid physics-ML parameterisation research
  • Large-model-dataset analysis and evaluation
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • International model consortia collaboration
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
